source.title: The rate-distortion function for source coding with side information at the decoder

confidence_rationale: Wyner-Ziv coding gives the minimum rate for sending X at a tolerated distortion when the decoder already holds correlated side information the encoder does not see. The required rate is a function of the receiver's side information, so the same source needs different rates to different receivers. That maps closely onto ARC-144's I_AB (what B needs minus what B can reconstruct locally) and its 'tolerated distortion' field. Held at 0.5 because it is a theorem about ideal codes with asymptotic block lengths and unbounded decoders, and gives no evidence that cognitive interfaces work this way.
failure_signatures: Asymptotic, unbounded-complexity coding: 'the receiver can reconstruct it from side information' in Wyner-Ziv means information-theoretically, which is weaker than ARC-144's cheap-and-reliable local reconstruction.
It shows rate is receiver-indexed for a single link; it says nothing about the size of any shared core across many links, which is ARC-144's falsifier.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The rate-distortion function for coding a source X when correlated side information Y is available only at the decoder is characterised; the minimum rate depends on Y and can be much lower than without it.
mapping.ree_translation: Take Y as what receiver B already holds or can compute. Then the rate A must send to B at a given tolerated distortion is R_AB(D), which depends on B. The contract entry {A -> B : I_AB, tolerated distortion, receiver capability} is close to a Wyner-Ziv problem statement, one per directed link.
mapping.mapping_caveat: ARC-144's 'cannot cheaply and reliably reconstruct' is a resource-bounded notion; Wyner-Ziv is resource-unbounded. ARC-144 also has fallback behaviour and latency, which the theorem ignores. Support is for the form of the contract entry, not for any empirical claim about REE.
mapping.source_context: Classical information-theory result founding distributed source coding; follow-on 1978 paper by Wyner extends to general sources.

confidence_components.notes: Metadata (venue, volume 22, issue 1, pp. 1-10, DOI) from WebSearch hits; IEEE page egress-blocked. Not named in the claim's notes; added as the most exact formal counterpart of I_AB.
